Pre-parkrun warm-up checklist (arrival 25–30 minutes before start): take SABA 5–15 minutes before starting warm-up; 6–8 minutes easy jog; 2–3 minutes dynamic drills; 4 strides of 20–30s with full recovery; quick bathroom/snack if needed; keep layered clothing on and remove layers as you warm up.

Use finishing time to set paces: 5K race pace = parkrun pace; tempo pace ≈ 15–30s slower per km than 5K pace; short intervals (1–2 min) faster than 5K pace (~3–8% faster); longer intervals (3–5 min) around to slightly slower than 5K pace depending on fatigue.
Track inhaler puffs used and symptoms; if more than usual or troublesome, discuss with GP about controller therapy or adjusting training.

Post-parkrun: cool-down 8–12 min easy jog/walk, gentle stretching or mobility, post-run snack carb + 15–25 g protein within 60 minutes, rest next day (active recovery), resume easy runs only if breathing and legs feel recovered.
If parkrun was strong and manageable: fine-tune interval target paces, continue tempo progression and targeted intervals (Weeks 9–12), aim for another race attempt in Week 11–12.

If parkrun caused excessive fatigue or significant asthma symptoms: repeat Week 8 training load or back off intensity for 1 week; reduce interval intensity and tempo duration; consult GP about symptoms and inhaler plan.

raw_text:
Below is the complete 12‑week Couch‑to‑5K program tailored for your 24‑year‑old client with exercise‑induced asthma (EIA) who uses a SABA inhaler. It integrates progressive base-building, intervals, a weekly tempo session, strength work (two sessions/week), paced progression, a Week‑8 parkrun test, and a race‑prep finisher week. Safety and asthma precautions are woven into every week: full warm‑ups, inhaler timing/use, extra warm-up/protection in cold air, and conservative progression. You can swap days to fit his schedule (just keep at least one easy day between hard sessions).

Key reminders (read before following plan)
- Warm-up before every run and especially before tempo/interval sessions: 10–15 minutes (6–8 min easy jog + dynamic drills + 4–6 strides/build‑ups).
- Use SABA (short‑acting bronchodilator) prophylactically per his GP/prescription (commonly 5–15 min before higher intensity). Carry inhaler during all sessions and the parkrun/race.
- In cold weather: do warm‑up indoors if possible, cover mouth/nose, delay intense efforts until fully warm.
- Talk test: easy runs = conversational; tempo = short phrases; intervals = single words/short phrases.
- If asthma symptoms (wheeze/tightness) occur and don’t respond to inhaler, stop and seek medical care. Track inhaler use and symptoms.
- Frequency: 3 runs per week (Mon/Wed/Sat layout as default), 2 strength sessions/week (Strength A = full, Strength B = short), 1 rest day and 1 optional cross‑train day.
- Progression: increase run time and intensity gradually. If he can’t complete a week, repeat it rather than progress.

Warm-up template (every session; longer for hard sessions)
- 6–8 min easy jog
- Dynamic mobility (leg swings, walking lunges, hip circles) 2–3 min
- 4–6 strides/build‑ups 20–30s (before intervals/tempo/parkrun/race)
- Total warm‑up: 10–15 min (longer in cold)

Cool-down template
- 8–12 min easy jog/walk + light static stretch (calves, quads, hamstrings, glutes)

Strength structure
- Strength A (full) — 30–40 min once/week (glute bridges → goblet squats → split squats → RDLs → band lateral walk → calf raises → plank → Pallof press). 2–3 rounds early weeks, progress to 3–4 rounds later.
- Strength B (short) — 15–20 min once/week (single‑leg RDL → reverse lunges → lateral band walk → glute bridge → side plank → calf raises). 2 rounds.
- Progressions: increase sets, weight, single‑leg variations every 2–3 weeks. Avoid heavy loads within 72 hours of hard sessions.

Weekly layout (default)
- Mon: Easy run + Strength B (short) later or rest
- Tue: Rest or active recovery/cross‑train
- Wed: Interval session (progressive)
- Thu: Strength A (full) or rest (light)
- Fri: Rest or easy jog/mobility
- Sat: Long run / tempo / parkrun / race depending on week
- Sun: Rest / active recovery

RPE guide
- Easy: 3–4/10, conversational
- Steady/long: 5–6/10
- Tempo: 7–8/10, short phrases only
- Intervals: 8–9/10 (shorter = faster)

12‑Week Plan (week‑by‑week summary)
Week 1 — Base & routine
- Mon: Warm-up → 1 min run / 2 min walk x10 → cool-down. Strength B (short) optional.
- Wed: 1.5–2 min easy run/walk session (as tolerated; see warm-up).
- Sat: 20–25 min easy continuous walk/run mix; 4 strides at end.
- Strength A: Start light this week if comfortable (or in Week 2).

Week 2 — Slight increase
- Mon: Warm-up → 1.5 min run / 2 min walk x8 → cool-down. Strength B (short).
- Wed: Easy 20–25 min run/walk mix.
- Sat: 25–30 min easy session + 4 strides.
- Strength A: Light technique focus.

Week 3 — More continuous running
- Mon: Warm-up → 3 min run / 2 min walk x6 → cool-down. Strength B.
- Wed: 20–25 min easy run.
- Sat: 25–30 min easy run with strides.
- Strength A: technique and moderate load.

Week 4 — Consolidation, pickups introduced
- Mon: Warm-up → 5 min run / 3 min walk x4 → cool-down. Strength B.
- Wed: Easy 25 min + 4 strides.
- Sat: 30 min continuous easy run or 20–25 min continuous if still adapting.
- Strength A: build slightly (2–3 rounds).

Week 5 — Tempo intro + intervals start
- Mon: Easy 25–30 min + 4 strides; Strength B.
- Wed: Interval intro: Warm-up → 8 x 1 min hard with 2–3 min recovery → cool-down.
- Sat (Tempo intro): Warm-up → 2 x 4 min tempo (3 min recovery) → cool-down. Total tempo ≈8 min.
- Strength A: moderate (3 rounds).

Week 6 — Increase continuous time & interval length
- Mon: Easy 25–30 min + strides; Strength B.
- Wed: Intervals: Warm-up → 6–8 x 90s at near-tempo/5K-ish with 2–3 min recovery → cool-down.
- Sat: 22–28 min continuous run or 25 min steady.
- Strength A: increase load if technique good.

Week 7 — Build tempo & 5K pace reps
- Mon: 30 min easy + strides; Strength B.
- Wed: Mixed intervals: 4 x 400–600m (or 90–120s) faster-than-5K pace, 2–3 min recovery; then 2 x 3 min at controlled 5K pace, 2 min recovery. Cool-down.
- Sat (Tempo): Warm-up → 12 min continuous tempo (or 2 x 6 min) → cool-down.
- Strength A: moderate.

Week 8 — Parkrun test week (use parkrun on Sat)
- Mon: Easy 30–35 min + 4 strides; Strength B light.
- Wed: Intervals: Warm-up → 8–10 x 1 min hard (90–120s recovery) → cool-down. (Keep this at least 72 hrs before parkrun.)
- Thu: Strength A (reduced load)
- Fri: Rest or easy 20–25 min jog + mobility
- Sat: parkrun (5K) — full warm‑up 12–20 min, conservative start, even pacing, cool‑down 8–12 min.
- Sun: Rest / active recovery.
- Use parkrun time to set paces for remainder of plan.

Week 9 — Use parkrun data; race-pace intervals
- Mon: Easy 25–30 min + strides; Strength B.
- Wed: Intervals: Warm-up → 5 x 4 min at slightly faster than 5K pace with 2–3 min recovery → cool-down.
- Sat: 5K time trial (or 30–35 min steady run if not ready).
- Strength A: light/moderate.

Week 10 — Threshold & sharpening
- Mon: Easy 25–30 min + strides; Strength B.
- Wed: Mixed session: Warm-up → 3 x (3 min at 5K pace + 2 min easy) then 6 x 1 min faster-than-5K with 90–120s recovery → cool-down.

Progression, adjustments and safety
- If he fails to complete a week comfortably, repeat that week rather than progress.
- Increase interval intensity/pace only if breathing and recovery are good; otherwise extend recovery times or reduce reps.
- In cold weather or high pollen, consider treadmill/indoor track for intervals and tempo.
- Track inhaler puffs per session. If inhaler use increases over multiple weeks or he has troublesome symptoms, consult GP about controller options.
- Avoid heavy leg strength (high load, high volume) within 72 hours of key sessions (intervals/tempo/race).

Nutrition & recovery (summary)
- Pre-hard session snack: small carb 60–90 min before (banana/toast/yogurt).
- Post-session: carb + protein within 60 minutes (e.g., chocolate milk, yogurt + fruit) to aid recovery.
- Aim for 7–9 hours sleep, regular meals with adequate carbs/fats/protein. Protein target ~1.2–1.6 g/kg/day for fitness adaptation.
- Hydrate regularly; avoid excessive caffeine before intense sessions if it worsens palpitations (SABA can cause palpitations in some).

Record keeping and monitoring
- Keep a simple log per session: date, workout, distance/time, inhaler puffs (pre/during/post), symptoms (wheeze/chest tightness), perceived effort, and notes. This helps you and his GP decide if adjustments or medication changes are needed.
